claims.statement: The European Commission identifies a complex customer journey, installer shortages, waiting periods, financing limits, and installation cost as barriers to heat-pump deployment, and estimates that 750000 additional installers are needed for 2030 goals.

EPREL is an EU-operated product database covering energy and environmental performance of labelled consumer and B2B products, including heating equipment, and exposes product information for purchasing decisions.

contrary_evidence: Large wholesalers and manufacturers may already provide proprietary sizing or quoting tools.
Installers may prefer familiar spreadsheets because liability remains with them.

economics.acquisition_route: Prove quote-time and error reduction in the family business, then approach one regional wholesaler with an embedded pilot tied to cart conversion.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 25 EU wholesalers at 300000 PLN annual recurring revenue each produce 7.5m PLN ARR; at 30% EBITDA, 4x EBITDA, and 65% founder ownership, equity is about 5.9m PLN in year 6-8, excluding retained cash as a second count.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: 15-20 hours weekly during the first integration, falling after reusable connectors and validation rules exist.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 78-88% after model inference and support; catalog onboarding is charged separately to avoid services drag.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 30000-60000 PLN enterprise acquisition and integration cost recovered within 6-12 months per live wholesaler.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 50000-120000 PLN implementation plus 8-20 PLN per completed configuration, or a 12000-30000 PLN monthly minimum per wholesaler.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Catalog and commerce integration create annual contracts; every installer order is a repeat usage event.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Observed substitutions, incompatibilities, returned items, and winning configurations improve rules and recommendations by local market
fingerprint.customer: Small renewable and HVAC installers buying equipment through wholesalers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Renewable and electrical wholesalers expose the copilot inside portals repeatedly used by their installer accounts
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Embedded configuration, BOM, quote, and documentation API sold as transaction-enablement SaaS
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Wholesaler pays a platform fee plus usage for each completed configuration or converted cart
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An installer must turn incomplete building information into a compatible, available, compliant equipment basket and quote

founder_fit: The family installation business can test outputs against real quotes without cold consumer acquisition.
Constraint solving, document extraction, and AI-assisted quoting fit the founder's technical profile.
Wholesaler distribution concentrates sales into a small number of accounts and supports part-time operation.
risks: Incorrect sizing or compatibility advice can cause costly rework.
Wholesaler integrations may have long procurement cycles.
Manufacturer rules and subsidy documentation change across countries.

structure.control_point: Compatible product graph joined to live catalog, availability, and quote workflow
structure.critical_dependency: A wholesaler willing to expose catalog and order-conversion data

thesis: Embed a Polish-first configuration copilot inside renewable and electrical wholesalers' ordering portals. It converts property inputs and installer preferences into a compatible bill of materials, editable assumptions, customer quote, product-data sheets, and a cart. The wholesaler has repeated access to installers and benefits from larger baskets, fewer compatibility returns, and installer loyalty; the product earns platform and usage fees rather than competing for end-customer leads.
title: Wholesaler-Embedded Heat-Pump and PV Configuration Copilot
uncertainties: Which product category creates enough configuration pain to win a first wholesaler?
Can catalog, availability, and price data be accessed in near real time?
Will the wholesaler accept vendor-neutral recommendations when it has inventory incentives?
